Journalism and AI:
Addressing Fears, Anxieties, and Concerns
Wednesday, October 28, 2026
10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET
Free to attend
In this webinar panel, three seasoned journalists —
Taylor Lorenz
,
Alexandra Marvar
, and
Brian Merchant
— will share how media workers can navigate AI tools and the various ways in which this technology has transformed the industry.
This panel will touch upon how legacy media outlets are coming up with AI rules, and what writers can do to protect their work. In addition, the panelists will discuss larger questions about how AI has changed the industry: Is it possible to integrate these tools in a workflow without plagiarizing other writers' work? Is there a double standard of media outlets banning freelancers from using these tools, while editors use in-house AI tools? What does it mean to have original prose in a time when LLMs can mimic style?
Register
here
.

episode

has no bylines.

Tobias Carroll Interviewed An Author About Vibe Coding and Poetry
For
Literary Hub
, Tobias Carroll interviewed the author Vikram Chandra.  Carroll told
Study Hall,
"A decade ago, Chandra's book
Geek Sublime
offered a thoughtful look at the ways in which writing code can be as elegant as poetry or prose. With AI-assisted coding on the rise, I talked with Chandra about how these changes in the tech world affected his book's central argument."
Brittany Kooienga Profiled Women Who Fell In Love With Their Meals Again After Getting Divorced
For
Food & Wine
, Brittany Kooienga wrote about "women finding freedom in deciding what to have for dinner without a romantic partner's input. For many women, the mental load of meal planning for someone else's preferences became a burden in their relationships." Kooienga told
Study Hall
, "Food became an unexpected joy for many women after their divorce."
